text.p: Following are the main stories in Friday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Malaysian government will conduct a comprehensive study of non-governmental organisations in the country to ensure that they are not exploited by "a few individuals", said Deputy Home Minister Megat Junid Megat Ayub.

-- Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad arrived in Los Angeles on Monday for a week-long visit to promote the Multimedia Super Corridor, a 15-by -60 kilometre zone extending south from Kuala Lumpur. Mahathir is scheduled to have meetings with the chief executives of several technology-related companies.

-- The New Straits Times Press (Malaysia) Bhd is seeking the approval of shareholders for the proposed disposal of its 20.13 percent stake in Commerce Asset Holdings Bhd. The stake is being sold for around 900 million ringgit.
-- Berjaya Group Bhd is looking to sell its entire shareholdings in three packaging companies for a total of 26 million ringgit.

-- Power utility Tenaga Nasional Bhd and Malaysian Resources Corporation Bhd have almost completed the second power purchase agreement for the Segari Energy Ventures power plant, said Tenaga executive chairman Ahmad Tajuddin Ali.
